report:
## Conclusion: True (with an important limit)

Kyleena (19.5 mg levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) is FDA-labeled/approved in the U.S. **to prevent pregnancy for up to five years**. The FDA prescribing label explicitly says it is “indicated for prevention of pregnancy for up to 5 years.” [https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/208224Orig1s002lbl.pdf](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/208224Orig1s002lbl.pdf)

The evidence supporting that duration includes the pivotal contraceptive-efficacy study: 1,452 generally healthy participants aged 18–35 received Kyleena. The official label reports a five-year cumulative pregnancy rate of about **1.45 per 100 users** (approximately 98.6% effectiveness over five years). [https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080)

The main qualification—and the evidence against reading the claim more broadly—is that **“up to five years” is not approval for use beyond five years**. If contraception is still wanted at that point, the labeled guidance is to remove and replace the system; this differs from some other IUD products that have longer approved durations. [https://www.kyleenahcp.com/resources/iud-faqs](https://www.kyleenahcp.com/resources/iud-faqs)

Pregnancy can occur rarely during use, and a pregnancy with Kyleena in place needs prompt medical assessment because of ectopic-pregnancy risk.
